Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG exchange and upcoming SOC2 evidence pull, Finx needs a concise package showing your vulnerability management rhythm and how you handle high-impact CVEs. Specifically we need: 

- Weekly authenticated scan outputs (last 4 weeks) or an automated feed
- Stated SLA for critical (CVSS 9.0-10.0) vulnerabilities and examples of closure timelines
- A simple owner roster showing who receives escalations for triage and for change windows

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide weekly scan PDFs and a roster spreadsheet, and also whether you have a documented emergency patch SLA (hours to mitigation or compensating control)? Our audit window is the week of Jun 25.

Best,
Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Confirming we can provide the items and will bundle them into a single package for your SIG/SOC2 window. Quick notes on scope and what we'll attach: 

- Weekly scans: we'll export the authenticated weekly scan results (PDF) for the last 4 runs and include the job metadata (scanner version, auth token hash).
- Emergency SLA: Redwood's published policy is 72 hours for Critical (CVSS >= 9.0) full remediation where a code/patch is required; we provide compensating controls or mitigations within 24 hours (e.g., WAF rule, network ACL, runtime block) while patch work is scheduled. For the audit, we'll include a short attestation and two anonymized examples of a recent Critical CVE closure timeline.
- Ownership roster: attached an ownership matrix (who triages, who owns patch windows, who signs off on exceptions).

I'll put together the package and share via a secure link (DocuSign-style artifact link) by Jun 21 COB. If you need a real-time walkthrough, Marissa (CS) and Evelyn (SecOps) can join the call.

Action items:

- Marissa: coordinate delivery and any procurement-facing statements if needed
- Evelyn: confirm the 72/24 SLA language for our attestation

Thanks,

Emily / team — attaching the short attestation language we will sign for your SIG intake. This reflects our operational practice and the controls we apply for production inference clusters. Highlights:

- Scan cadence: authenticated vulnerability scans run weekly, automated reporting to our asset inventory; results retained for 12 months.
- SLA: for Critical CVEs (CVSS 9.0–10.0) we commit to providing measurable compensating controls within 24 hours and targeted remediation (patch or mitigation) within 72 hours when a code/update is available. For Critical CVEs requiring coordinated upstream fixes, we provide documented mitigation plans and status updates at 24/48/72 hour marks.
- Exceptions: any extension beyond 72 hours is routed through an exception ticket; business-impacting exceptions are approved by Security Leadership (cc'ed Markus).

We will include two redacted closure timelines (one public dependency, one internal component) that show our patch window and verification steps.

On the attached roster: primary triage is handled by our On-Call SecOps (listed), patch scheduling by Platform Engineering, and final acceptance by Product Security. Names and on-call rotations are in ownership_roster-2028-06.xlsx.

If that language looks good to you, Jonas will share the artifact bundle.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
